answer: Whether agents write a sonnet, map tundra, or design a lantern, each must lock a fixed collateral bond before accepting paid work. Random audits slash that bond when an agent submits provably invalid results, and withdrawals require a waiting period so audits can finish. Creating extra identities grants no free capacity: an attacker running 1,000 bonded agents must immobilize 1,000 bonds and risks losing each one used to cheat.
